userStories.title: Image attachments from bytes and labels
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Convert sniffed bytes into bounded ImageAttachment values and shared image labels, exported through the chat barrel.

**Motivation** — Feature 1 made images travel from `AgentSession.send` to the model and to disk, but nothing in chat can create one.

**Approach** — `image-sniff.ts` holds `ImageFormat`, `SniffedImage` and `sniffImage`; `image-file.ts` holds the rest and imports `./image-sniff`; `index.ts` re-exports both. Code outside the folder (`@/chat` itself, `mention-expand.ts`) imports through the `index.ts` barrel.

`imageFromBytes` checks in this order, first failure wins: `sniffImage` returns undefined → `not a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image`; the base64 length `Math.ceil(bytes.length / 3) * 4` is over `MAX_IMAGE_BASE64_CHARS` (`@nathapp/nax-agent`, 5,242,880, so 3,932,160 raw bytes is the largest accepted) → `image is larger than 3.75 MiB`; `width` or `height` over `MAX_IMAGE_EDGE_PX` → `image is larger than 8000 px on a side`. Otherwise it returns `{ image: { mimeType, data: <base64 of bytes>, width?, height?, source } }`, `width` and `height` present only when sniffed.

Labels: `imageRawBytes` is `data.length / 4 * 3` minus the number of trailing `=`. `imageSizeLabel(bytes)` is `${Math.max(1, Math.floor(bytes / 1024))} KB` below 1,048,576 bytes, else `${(bytes / 1_048_576).toFixed(1)} MB`. `imageDescription` joins `imageFormatOf(mimeType)`, `<width>×<height>` (only when both are present; `×` is U+00D7) and the size label with ` · `. `imageNoteLabel(n, image)` is `image <n> · <imageDescription>` followed by ` · <source>` when `source` is present.

**Scope** — In: image-file.ts, images/index.ts, exports from src/chat/index.ts and unit behavior. Out: sniffer implementation (US-001), mention integration (US-006), transcript layout (US-009) and resizing, cropping or re-encoding images.

**Interface**
```ts
import type { ImageAttachment } from "@nathapp/nax-agent";
export const MAX_IMAGE_EDGE_PX = 8000;
export function imageFromBytes(bytes: Uint8Array, source: string): { readonly image: ImageAttachment } | { readonly refusal: string };
export function imageFormatOf(mimeType: string): string;          // "png" | "jpeg" | "gif" | "webp", else "image"
export function imageRawBytes(image: ImageAttachment): number;     // decoded size of image.data
export function imageSizeLabel(bytes: number): string;             // "342 KB", "1.5 MB"
export function imageDescription(image: ImageAttachment): string;  // "png · 1280×720 · 342 KB"
export function imageNoteLabel(number: number, image: ImageAttachment): string; // "image 1 · png · 1280×720 · 342 KB · clipboard"
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] imageFromBytes on a valid 1280×720 PNG with source 'clipboard' returns { image } whose mimeType is 'image/png', data is the base64 of the bytes, width is 1280, height is 720 and source is 'clipboard'.
[unit] imageFromBytes on the bytes of 'hello' returns { refusal: 'not a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image' }.
[unit] imageFromBytes on a PNG of exactly 3,932,160 bytes returns { image }, and on a PNG of 3,932,161 bytes returns { refusal: 'image is larger than 3.75 MiB' }.
[unit] imageFromBytes on a PNG declaring width 8000 returns { image }, and on one declaring width 8001 (or height 8001) returns { refusal: 'image is larger than 8000 px on a side' }.
[unit] imageFromBytes on a PNG of 3,932,161 bytes that also declares width 9000 returns the size refusal 'image is larger than 3.75 MiB', because the size check runs before the edge check.
[unit] imageRawBytes returns 3 for an image whose data is 'AAAA' and 1 for 'AA=='.
[unit] imageSizeLabel(350_208) returns '342 KB', imageSizeLabel(100) returns '1 KB', imageSizeLabel(1_048_575) returns '1023 KB', and imageSizeLabel(1_572_864) returns '1.5 MB'.
[unit] imageDescription of a PNG image with width 1280, height 720 and 350,208 raw bytes returns 'png · 1280×720 · 342 KB'; without width and height it returns 'png · 342 KB'.
[unit] imageNoteLabel(2, image) for that PNG with source 'clipboard' returns 'image 2 · png · 1280×720 · 342 KB · clipboard'; with no source it returns 'image 2 · png · 1280×720 · 342 KB'.
[unit] imageFormatOf('image/jpeg') returns 'jpeg' and imageFormatOf('image/bmp') returns 'image'.

[unit] sniffImage, imageFromBytes, imageNoteLabel and MAX_IMAGE_EDGE_PX (equal to 8000) are importable from @/chat and usable, and imageFromBytes on a PNG with no IHDR (signature only) returns an image with no width or height, because its format comes from sniffImage.

routing.reasoning: Deterministic byte validation, base64 arithmetic, labels and barrel additions over existing image constants.

userStories.title: Pasted image paths
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Recognize pasted image file paths without filesystem access and allow ChatInput to intercept multi-code-point pasted chunks.

**Motivation** — A pasted path is inserted as text.

**Approach** — `pastedImagePath(chunk: string, cwd: string): string | undefined` is pure (no filesystem). It trims the chunk; an empty chunk or one holding a newline is `undefined`. A chunk starting `file://` becomes the URL's decoded pathname, and a `file://` chunk that does not parse as a URL or whose percent-decoding fails is `undefined` (never a throw: the function runs inside the input's key handler); a chunk wrapped in matching single or double quotes loses them; otherwise each backslash escape `\x` becomes `x`. The result must end in `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif` or `.webp` (case-insensitive), else `undefined`. It returns the path resolved against `cwd` (an absolute path stays as is). Whether the file exists and is an image is decided later, by reading it.

`ChatInput` gains an optional prop `onPaste?: (chunk: string) => boolean`. Its `useInput` handler calls it before `editLine` when the input holds more than one code point and neither `key.ctrl`, `key.meta` nor `key.return` is set; when it returns `true` the chunk is not inserted. A single typed character never reaches it.

**Scope** — In: pasted-path.ts, optional onPaste prop and input interception, pure parser and mounted ChatInput tests. Out: asynchronous file reads/fallback insertion/ChatApp wiring (US-010), /image command parsing (US-011), and `~` expansion in pasted paths and in `/image <path>`. Keep InputDraft and line-editor pure and unchanged.

**Interface**
```ts
export function pastedImagePath(chunk: string, cwd: string): string | undefined;
// Added to ChatInputProps:
readonly onPaste?: (chunk: string) => boolean;
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] pastedImagePath('/Users/me/Desktop/shot.png', '/repo') returns '/Users/me/Desktop/shot.png'.
[unit] pastedImagePath('  /tmp/a.PNG \n', '/repo') returns '/tmp/a.PNG': whitespace and the trailing newline are trimmed and the extension check ignores case.
[unit] pastedImagePath on a matching single-quoted or double-quoted '/tmp/my shot.png', with cwd '/repo', returns '/tmp/my shot.png' in both cases.
[unit] pastedImagePath returns '/tmp/my shot.png' for cwd '/repo' and a chunk consisting of '/tmp/my', one literal backslash, and ' shot.png'.
[unit] pastedImagePath('file:///tmp/my%20shot.jpg', '/repo') returns '/tmp/my shot.jpg'.
[unit] pastedImagePath('shots/a.webp', '/repo') returns '/repo/shots/a.webp'.
[unit] pastedImagePath('/tmp/a.txt', '/repo') returns undefined, and so do pastedImagePath('hello world', '/repo') and pastedImagePath('', '/repo').
[unit] pastedImagePath('/tmp/a.png\n/tmp/b.png', '/repo') returns undefined because the trimmed chunk holds a newline.
[unit] pastedImagePath('file:///tmp/%zz.png', '/repo') and pastedImagePath('file://', '/repo') return undefined without throwing.
[unit] pastedImagePath accepts the extensions .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif and .webp, and returns undefined for .bmp.
[integration] A ChatInput with an onPaste that returns true, sent the chunk /tmp/a.png on stdin, calls onPaste once with '/tmp/a.png' and leaves the editor text empty.
[integration] A ChatInput with an onPaste that returns false, sent the chunk hello, calls onPaste with 'hello' and shows hello in the editor.
[integration] A ChatInput with an onPaste, sent the single character a, never calls onPaste and shows a.
[integration] A ChatInput without onPaste, sent the chunk hello, shows hello as it does today.

routing.reasoning: Pure path normalization plus a small optional input callback and mounted component assertions; no file effects or capability decisions.

userStories.title: Mentioned images
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expand image mentions into ordered attachments on image-capable brains while preserving existing path-only behavior and repo boundaries otherwise.

**Motivation** — An `@shot.png` mention sends only its path (`mention-expand.ts` `contentRecord`, `PATH_ONLY_BINARY`).

**Approach** —
- `MentionStatus` gains `"image"`; the envelope's `MENTION_STATUSES` accepts it.
- `MentionWhere` gains `images?: boolean` (absent = false).
- `ExpandedMentions` gains `images?: readonly ImageAttachment[]`, present when non-empty.
- `contentRecord`: after reading the bytes and before the binary check, when `sniffImage(bytes)` is an image: with `where.images` not true the record is `path-only` with note `path only: model cannot read images`; otherwise `imageFromBytes(bytes, located.path)`; a refusal is `path-only` with note `path only: <refusal>`; success is `{ path, status: "image", note: "image · " + imageDescription(image), body: "" }` and the image is collected in mention order. Existing steps before it (resolve, boundary, ignored, folder, the 8 MiB read limit) are unchanged.
- `attachmentExpandable("image")` is false.

The image attachment label uses the existing formatMentionToken convention: attachmentLabel for the image case returns `attached @shot.png · image · png · 2×3 · 1 KB` for the AC's record (the AC's @-prefixed path is authoritative). Modules outside images/ import its index barrel; mention-expand.ts should not import the chat root back into its own barrel.

Capability: `ChatHost.acceptsImages?()` asks the open session (`session.acceptsImages?.()`, from feature 1). A brain that cannot read images refuses a send that has placeholder images, keeps the draft and says why. A mentioned image on such a brain degrades to today's path-only record instead of refusing the send, so `@` mentions on a text-only model behave as before. (**Claude** call.) This story consumes where.images; it does not query the host.

**Scope** — In: mention types/envelope/expander and image attachment label, image recognition before the binary check, ordered optional images collection, existing highlighting behavior. Out: host capability lookup (US-007), send-level capability decision (US-012), standalone transcript image rows (US-009), and checking a mentioned image against the brain's capability per image beyond the yes/no acceptsImages answer.

**Interface**
```ts
// Add "image" to MentionStatus.
// Add to MentionWhere:
readonly images?: boolean;
// Add to ExpandedMentions:
readonly images?: readonly ImageAttachment[];
```
Modify src/chat/mentions/types.ts, mention-envelope.ts, mention-expand.ts and src/tui/chat/layout-attachment.ts. mentionTranscriptEntries already highlights every non-refused status; preserve it.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] expandChatMentions('see @shot.png', { cwd, repoRoot, images: true }), with the deps returning PNG bytes for shot.png, returns a record { path: 'shot.png', status: 'image', note: 'image · png · 2×3 · 1 KB', body: '' }.

[unit] expandChatMentions('see @shot.png', { cwd, repoRoot, images: true }), with deps returning a 2×3 PNG for shot.png, returns images holding one ImageAttachment with mimeType 'image/png', data the base64 of the file bytes, width 2, height 3 and source 'shot.png'.

[unit] A mentioned PNG of 3,932,161 bytes with images: true returns a path-only record with note 'path only: image is larger than 3.75 MiB' and no images key.
[unit] A mentioned file named notes.png whose bytes are UTF-8 text with no NUL byte is attached as text with status attached, because the format comes from the bytes.
[unit] A mentioned file named photo.dat holding JPEG bytes, with images: true, returns status image and an image/jpeg attachment.
[unit] Two image mentions @a.png @b.gif with images: true return images in the order a, b.
[unit] A mentioned image outside the repo is refused as today ('not attached: outside the repo') and adds no image.
[unit] The expanded message for an image mention parses back with parseMentionMessage into the typed text and a record whose status is image and whose body is ''.
[unit] parseMentionMessage on an envelope whose record says status="image" returns that record.
[unit] attachmentLabel({ path: 'shot.png', status: 'image', note: 'image · png · 2×3 · 1 KB' }) returns 'attached @shot.png · image · png · 2×3 · 1 KB'.

`MENTION_STATUSES` accepts `"image"`.

`attachmentLabel` gains the `image` case (its switch has no default); `image` is not expandable.

userStories.title: Image rows in the transcript and on replay
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Render nonexpandable image note entries consistently for live sent messages and stored history, including missing-image notes.

**Motivation** — Typical uses: a screenshot of a broken TUI render, a web page, an error dialog.

**Approach** —
- `TranscriptEntry` gains `{ kind: "image"; label: string }`, laid out as one muted row behind the result prefix (`cardRows`, as an attachment row's label is), never expandable.
- `sentEntries(message, images?)` (`mention-send.ts`): the entries it returns today, followed by `{ kind: "image", label: imageNoteLabel(i + 1, image) }` for the first `k` images, where `k` = `max(0, images.length − <number of image-status records in the parsed mention envelope>)` (mention images come last and already have their attachment row). On replay, when an image was dropped as missing, this count can cover one image fewer than was sent; the `image · missing` row still shows.
- Replay (`history-replay.ts`): a stored user message first loses each trailing line that is exactly `[image missing]` (feature 1's load note). The rest replays as `sentEntries(content, message.images)` does, and each removed line adds `{ kind: "image", label: "image · missing" }` after those entries.

Preserve existing compaction notices and skill/mention replay behavior; content empty after stripping yields no blank user entry. Add layout-image.ts and the image branch in layout.ts, without adding expand/click state.

**Scope** — In: transcript-model.ts union, layout.ts dispatch/new layout-image.ts, mention-send.ts image rows and history-replay.ts stored images/missing lines. Out: mention expansion (US-006), screen send integration (US-013), screen live sentEntries arguments/reset (US-014), terminal image drawing and expanding an image note row to show more (the row already names its source).

**Interface**
```ts
// TranscriptEntry gains:
{ kind: "image"; label: string }
// Existing function gains optional input:
sentEntries(message: string, images?: readonly ImageAttachment[])
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] layoutTranscript of [{ kind: 'image', label: 'image 1 · png · 2×3 · 1 KB · clipboard' }] draws one row holding that label behind the result prefix, in the muted color.

[unit] sentEntries('look [Image #1]', [image]), for a PNG image of width 2, height 3, source 'clipboard' and a payload below 2,048 raw bytes, returns [{ kind: 'user', text: 'look [Image #1]' }, { kind: 'image', label: 'image 1 · png · 2×3 · 1 KB · clipboard' }].

userStories.title: Attaching images in the chat screen
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Own image-draft effects in useImageAttach and wire active Ctrl+v and pasted paths into ChatApp without losing asynchronous edits.

**Motivation** — The clipboard module is write-only (`packages/nax/src/tui/chat/clipboard.ts`), ctrl+v is ignored by the line editor (`line-editor.ts` `ctrlResult`), a pasted path is inserted as text.

**Approach** — The module exports `_imageAttachDeps = { readClipboard: readClipboardImage, readFile: (path: string) => Promise<Uint8Array | undefined> }` (read at call time, so tests replace its members with `spyOn`) and the hook `useImageAttach(options: { cwd; input: RefObject<ChatInputHandle | undefined>; editor: () => EditorState; notice: (text: string) => void; active: () => boolean })`, which returns `{ current(): ImageDraft; onPaste(chunk: string): boolean; attach(path?: string): Promise<void>; restore(draft: ImageDraft): void; reset(): void }`. `attach()` with no path is the clipboard flow; `options.editor` returns the newest editor state, from a ref ChatApp updates in `changeDraft`, so an attach that finishes after an `await` inserts into the text as it stands then, not as it stood at the key press. Attaches run one at a time in the order they were asked for: a ctrl+v or paste that arrives while a read is in flight waits for it. The hook owns the `ImageDraft` (state plus a ref for batched keys). The default `readFile` reads at most 3,932,161 bytes (one over the image limit, so an oversized file still meets the size refusal without being read whole) and resolves `undefined` when the path does not exist, is not a regular file, or cannot be read. It writes placeholders into the prompt through the input handle's existing `edit(state)` (`ChatInputHandle`), and notices through ChatApp's `append({ kind: "notice", text })`.

- **ctrl+v** (`key.ctrl` and input `v`), while the input is active (no ask card, no picker): `readClipboard()`. `image` → `imageFromBytes(bytes, "clipboard")` → `attachToDraft`. `none` → notice `no image on the clipboard`. `unsupported` → `pasting images needs macOS or Linux; use /image <path>`. `failed` → `could not read the clipboard: <reason>`.
- **Paste**: `onPaste(chunk)` returns `true` when `pastedImagePath(chunk, cwd)` is a path, and then reads it. A path pasted into a line that starts with `/` is attached like any other, and the later submit is refused by the slash-line rule (see Sending). A file that `readFile` cannot find, or bytes that are not an image, put the original chunk into the prompt at the cursor as text, so a normal paste is never lost. Any other refusal is a notice and nothing is inserted.
- **`/image [path]`**: `runSlashCommand` returns the new outcome `{ kind: "attach"; path?: string }` (`path` = `command.rest` trimmed, absent when empty) and ChatApp hands it to the hook. No path → the ctrl+v flow. A path → `readFile(resolve(cwd, path))`: `undefined` → notice `image not found: <path>`; otherwise as a paste, except that a non-image is the notice `image not attached: <refusal>`. `image` is added to `COMMANDS` right after `plugins`, described `Attach an image to the next message`. It is a builtin with no ACP-owned feature, so it works on ACP brains too. Like every other command it waits while a turn runs.
- Except for a pasted non-image, which reinserts the original chunk as text with no notice, every refusal from `imageFromBytes` or `attachToDraft` is the notice `image not attached: <refusal>`.
- Sources: `clipboard` for the clipboard, the absolute path for a paste or `/image <path>`, the typed path for an `@` mention.

ctrl+v with no image on the clipboard shows `no image on the clipboard`; nax does not try to paste clipboard text (the design left this to the builder; a terminal never pastes text on ctrl+v, so the hint cannot follow a text paste).

**Scope** — In: new use-image-attach.ts hook and _imageAttachDeps defaults, serialized clipboard/path reads, immutable draft composition, current-editor insertion/fallback, restore/reset primitives, and ChatApp hook/ctrl+v/onPaste/editor-ref wiring only. Out: /image slash registration and outcome wiring (US-011; hook attach(path) is ready here), send preparation/restoration (US-012/013), after-send reset (US-014), clipboard text pasting, attach-time brain capability checks, and reducing ChatApp.tsx or ChatInput.tsx below their existing size.

**Interface**
```ts
export const _imageAttachDeps = {
  readClipboard: readClipboardImage,
  readFile: (path: string) => Promise<Uint8Array | undefined>
};
// Hook options/return contract (typed members as described above):
useImageAttach(options: { cwd; input: RefObject<ChatInputHandle | undefined>; editor: () => EditorState; notice: (text: string) => void; active: () => boolean })
// returns { current(): ImageDraft; onPaste(chunk: string): boolean; attach(path?: string): Promise<void>; restore(draft: ImageDraft): void; reset(): void }
```
Use concrete TypeScript types for cwd and the hook return; the spec's abbreviated shape above expresses the exact member contract, not executable initializer syntax.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Register the image slash builtin on every brain and dispatch its optional path to useImageAttach.

**Motivation** — The user wants image input in `nax chat` for parity with Claude Code and Codex (user, 2026-10-31).

**Approach** — **`/image [path]`**: `runSlashCommand` returns the new outcome `{ kind: "attach"; path?: string }` (`path` = `command.rest` trimmed, absent when empty) and ChatApp hands it to the hook. No path → the ctrl+v flow. A path → `readFile(resolve(cwd, path))`: `undefined` → notice `image not found: <path>`; otherwise as a paste, except that a non-image is the notice `image not attached: <refusal>`. `image` is added to `COMMANDS` right after `plugins`, described `Attach an image to the next message`. It is a builtin with no ACP-owned feature, so it works on ACP brains too. Like every other command it waits while a turn runs.

- Every refusal from `imageFromBytes` or `attachToDraft` during `/image` is the notice `image not attached: <refusal>`; unlike a pasted non-image, a non-image supplied to this slash command never falls back to text insertion.
- Sources: `clipboard` for the clipboard, the absolute path for a paste or `/image <path>`, the typed path for an `@` mention.

`packages/nax/test/ui/chat/slash-commands.test.tsx` — "AC-4 never sends original /%s" iterates `COMMANDS` and so now submits the image command, which would run the real clipboard command; `mount()` stubs `_imageAttachDeps.readClipboard` (resolving `{ kind: "none" }`) so no test spawns `osascript`, `wl-paste` or `xclip`. Its assertion (`send` not called) is unchanged. `/image` sits after `/plugins`, outside the `/mcp` … `/quit` run that `test/ui/chat/slash-commands.test.tsx` pins.

**Scope** — In: slash-commands.ts COMMANDS/descriptions/SlashOutcome/runSlashCommand, ChatApp attach-outcome branch, command UI tests and narrowly scoped menu regression update. Out: hook implementation (US-010), rejecting slash lines carrying present images (US-013), images with slash commands/skills/! shell lines, and `~` expansion in pasted paths and in `/image <path>`. The hook already supplies clipboard/path reads and notices.

**Interface**

userStories.title: After an image send
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Show live image transcript notes and reset image ownership after every plain send while retaining text-only history recall.

**Motivation** — Typical uses: a screenshot of a broken TUI render, a web page, an error dialog.

**Approach** — Every plain message that reaches `host.send` (on either path) resets the `ImageDraft` to `EMPTY_IMAGE_DRAFT`, so a draft whose placeholders were all deleted does not keep its numbers. Up-arrow history keeps text only: a recalled `[Image #N]` with no draft image behind it is plain text.

`sentEntries(message, images?)` (`mention-send.ts`): the entries it returns today, followed by `{ kind: "image", label: imageNoteLabel(i + 1, image) }` for the first `k` images, where `k` = `max(0, images.length − <number of image-status records in the parsed mention envelope>)` (mention images come last and already have their attachment row). On replay, when an image was dropped as missing, this count can cover one image fewer than was sent; the `image · missing` row still shows.

ChatApp.tsx — draw a sent message's rows with `sentEntries(message, images)` and reset the image draft after every plain message that reaches `host.send`. The transcript shows one note row per image, `image 1 · png · 1280×720 · 342 KB · clipboard`, live and on resume. This story wires US-009's row generation into the live send path; preserve expanded-mention payload propagation from US-013 and the original text-only InputDraft.history. Do not reset after a preparation refusal or accidentally reset a future draft at asynchronous turn completion: the reset boundary is the plain message reaching host.send.

**Scope** — In: ChatApp sentEntries images argument and universal plain-send reset, mounted transcript/history/next-number behavior, reset even when the invoked host.send rejects, and mentioned-image send regression. Out: pure sentEntries/replay implementation (US-009), preparation/capability/refusal algorithms (US-012/013), hook attachment algorithms (US-010), terminal image drawing and re-sending earlier images when switching brains.

**Interface**
```ts
sentEntries(message: string, images?: readonly ImageAttachment[])
// useImageAttach result already exposes:
reset(): void;
```

analysis:
This is an additive enhancement to existing nax chat, not a greenfield agent/image stack. Graph-first navigation was attempted but codebase-memory MCP is not exposed in this session; findings below come from direct reads and text searches rooted at /Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax. All fourteen binding stories run in packages/nax, with exactly the supplied dependency graph. No changes to nax-agent, nax-agent-acp or nax-ai, no releases and no new dependencies are required. The lower image-content-parts feature (#2758) is already present: packages/nax-agent/src/session/image-input.ts:4-13 defines MIME types, MAX_IMAGES_PER_MESSAGE=10, MAX_IMAGE_BASE64_CHARS=5_242_880, MAX_REQUEST_IMAGE_BASE64_CHARS=20_971_520 and SendInput; its validateImageAttachments at :36 returns the first failure in count, image-order, total-size order. The count reason for eleven images is 'Image count exceeds the limit of 10 images per message'. AgentSession already accepts send(message, input?) and optional acceptsImages at packages/nax-agent/src/session/agent-session-types.ts:199-201. Missing persisted images already append exact trailing '[image missing]' lines at packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/transcript-images.ts:193-200. Treat those APIs and storage conventions as read-only integration dependencies; import image types, validation and constants from @nathapp/nax-agent's root, never nax-ai directly.

Architecture and implementation sequence: US-001 creates a pure magic/header sniffer; US-002 layers validation, byte encoding and display labels on it and exports the images barrel through src/chat/index.ts. US-003 clipboard effects, US-004 pure pasted-path parsing/input interception, US-005 immutable image draft and US-007 host plumbing can start independently. US-006 extends existing mentions only after US-002; US-008 extends ACP recording/handoff after US-002; US-009 adds transcript/replay rows after US-002/006. US-010 composes US-002/003/004/005 into the effectful hook and minimal ChatApp wiring; US-011 connects /image to that hook; US-012 composes draft and mention results; US-013 connects preparation, capability checks and host calls after US-007/008/010/012; US-014 connects sent-image rows and reset/history behavior after US-009/013. Binding dependencies are not to be expanded just to serialize shared files: coordinate narrowly scoped edits to ChatApp.tsx among US-010/011/013/014 and to chat/index.ts among host/image work. New source modules keep the heavy logic out of already-large components.

Existing input path: packages/nax/src/tui/chat/ChatInput.tsx:44-52 holds InputDraft with editor, string history and optional browse, which stays unchanged. Its handle at :118-133 already supports complete/edit/submit. The latest draft ref at :510-515 and publish at :527-530 protect batched keypresses. submit at :581-589 clears the editor and records history BEFORE notifying ChatApp; refusal must therefore write submitted text back through handle.edit with a code-point end cursor, not merely leave React state unchanged. The useInput reducer at :613-633 presently calls editLine without a paste interceptor. Add the optional onPaste before editLine for multi-code-point unmodified non-return chunks; never route individual typed characters through it. packages/nax/src/tui/chat/line-editor.ts:137-152 ignores ctrl+v and :174-187 keeps editLine pure; do not add filesystem/clipboard operations there. Its cursor is a code-point index, so placeholders and fallback text must use code-point splicing, not UTF-16 slice offsets. US-004 trims before rejecting internal newlines: '/tmp/a.PNG \n' is accepted after trimming. file:// parsing and percent decoding must never escape as exceptions from the key handler; do not expand '~'.

Screen path: packages/nax/src/tui/chat/ChatApp.tsx:80-86 exposes _chatAppDeps.expandMentions. The screen owns draft, entries, input handle and sending ref at :169-185; ask/picker ownership and menu claims are computed at :205-266, and useInput at :269-281 currently handles ctrl+o and interrupt escape. Hook activation must honor ask cards, pickers and control locking without stealing unrelated keys. changeDraft at :440-444 must also update a latest-editor ref synchronously. useImageAttach owns separate ImageDraft state plus a ref and a serialized attachment queue. Resolve each asynchronous attachment against the newest editor after the read, preventing stale-cursor text loss and duplicate numbers under batched keys. Deps members must be looked up at call time for spyOn replacement. File reads cap allocation at 3_932_161 bytes and reject missing, unreadable and nonregular files as undefined. A pasted candidate that is missing or non-image must reinsert its original chunk, whereas slash/clipboard invalid-image flows produce notices. Avoid introducing a broad catch that converts an oversized pasted PNG into text; only missing/non-image falls back. Keep clipboard write behavior in clipboard.ts separate from the new read module (packages/nax/src/tui/chat/clipboard.ts:1-33).

Send path and compatibility: submit currently distinguishes slash/plain at packages/nax/src/tui/chat/ChatApp.tsx:363-380 and prepares mentions through mentionPrepare; sendTurn at :383-419 locks the turn, prepares, appends sentEntries and calls host.send with two arguments unless a distinct title requires options. mention-send.ts:28-56 contains needsMentionExpansion and existing mentionPrepare, and :59-62 parses skills and mentions for transcript rows. New preparation must preserve exact existing calls for text-only messages, including expandMentions(text, { cwd, repoRoot }) on text-only or capability-absent hosts. Only present known placeholders carry images; deleted placeholders do not count toward attachment limits or send payload. Deduplicate repeated placeholders, order by first appearance and rewrite all occurrences with a single consistent renumbering map; unknown/history-only placeholders remain literal. Mention attachments follow placeholder attachments. Capability is queried once per prepared send, with rejection/absence treated as false; placeholder images refuse while mentions degrade to path-only. Refusal restores original submitted text and the same image draft, not renumbered/expanded text. A slash-prefixed submitted line with a present image is refused before parsing dispatch, including /quit and ACP/catalog commands; with no present image command behavior remains unchanged. Plain-message sends reset the image draft whenever they reach host.send, even if all placeholders were deleted; do not reset on preparation refusal. US-013 handles preparation/restore/payload; US-014 owns image-row wiring and universal plain-send reset. The existing title/history remain the user's submitted text.

Host integration: packages/nax/src/chat/chat-host.ts:86-88 has title-only ChatSendOptions; :91-121 defines ChatHost. Despite the spec's illustrative ChatHostImpl name, the actual implementation is the unexported NativeChatHost at :142, constructed via createChatHost. Do not rename it or invent an exported ChatHostImpl: modify that implementation and test via createChatHost. send at :491-529 delegates to runChatTurn at :506 while maintaining listener, ledger, nested work and metadata. Limit this 586-line file's edits to ImageAttachment import, optional interface fields, a one-line capability delegation (and necessary helper import), and options.images pass-through; stay at or below 600 lines. Add sessionAcceptsImages separately, preserving the wrapped method's receiver and returning false without an open session. packages/nax/src/chat/turn-runner.ts:9-27 defines RunChatTurnOptions and :53-76 consumes session.send(message), records usage, handles asks, drains ledger and writes metadata. Select the two-argument call only for nonempty images; do not alter streaming/meta semantics. Optional members keep existing hand-built fake hosts compatible.

Mentions: packages/nax/src/chat/mentions/types.ts:10 defines the status union and :42 ExpandedMentions; mention-envelope.ts:28 and :105-117 allowlist parsed statuses. mention-expand.ts:25-28 defines MentionWhere; :121-135 builds ordered records; :138-150 resolves/deduplicates/bounds/ignore-checks before contentRecord at :195-202. Preserve realpath containment, .git exclusion, ignored-file behavior, folder handling and the existing 8 MiB read limit.
